speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe the onset of the swelling and pain in your right ring finger, and have you experienced any recent trauma or insect bites to that area?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did you hear a distinct "pop" or snapping sound at the moment of injury, and are you currently unable to actively extend the tip of your finger?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on the inability to flex the distal interphalangeal joint and the mechanism of injury, I suspect an avulsion fracture or tendon rupture. REQUEST TEST: X-Ray Right Hand

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: X-ray of the Right Hand: No bone fractures or dislocations visible. Soft tissue swelling noted around the distal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Student and active in sports, particularly football. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, numbness, or tingling in the affected finger. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: The mechanism of injury, specifically the forced extension causing the finger to get stuck, combined with the inability to flex the distal interphalangeal joint, is classic for a mallet finger injury. DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallet Finger

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
